doc.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998

title: Flying Hurricanes in the RAF and meeting Bing Crosby
summary: Flew for the RAF in Africa; on leave in London he played with Crosby, who got him transferred to the American forces.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah. Can we talk about your love of flying for a minute? You ended up going back?
I flew in the RAF yeah, during the war, yeah. At the beginning of it I flew for almost two years.
Now were you an American citizen?
So that’s why you could have.

I was on the cusp, no I had no choice. And I guess I’m a total aviation buff or whatever those words are. I mean I sold my airplane last year because I had a rather adventuresome acquisition of the land properties at Westchester Airport one night when it was rain, freezing snow, so I called my good friend and said I think I’d better hang it up. It’s funny I just saw, in the city where I was conducting I just saw a reunion of a photo recon squadron that flew in Britain and also flew in Africa. I didn’t know them at that time but we got to talking and found out that we’d been side by side in the desert running from Rommel, and we were all — they flew P-38s and that airplane was a disaster in the African desert because of the inline engine and the sand. They couldn’t keep it running.

I flew Hurricanes. A cloth airplane with a metal stabilizer, a metal wingtip, not much protection. We used to beg and borrow every piece of metal that we could put under our derrieres. I was only shot down once, I was in pretty good shape.
That’s amazing. And then you flew some for the United States, too.

Then I came, I did a show, I went back to England on leave because I’d heard so much about the Miller band. And I flew back to London – I got leave and flew to London to hear it, and I arrived there before the band had arrived yet. There were rumors naturally.

And I ran into Crosby, Bing Crosby, who said, “I’m doing a benefit tonight” well not a benefit, but, “I’m doing a USO show at this club tonight, why don’t you come and play a couple of tunes with me?” And I was a Flying Sergeant, and in RAF you didn’t go to quarters where the officers — you just didn’t step across that line. And I told this to Bing and he said “if you don’t go I don’t go, it’s very simple, so come and have dinner afterwards.” And he talked to some gruffy Admiral of the Royal Navy and another man by the name of Andy Cannon who ran the Air Transport Command that took supplies back and forth across the Atlantic for the American Air Corps at that time. And I couldn’t believe Bing. He said, “I don’t want this kid to get hurt,” when he found out where I was flying, it was very dangerous. And I went back to my squadron in Africa, and my backman was a Scotsman who said, and I can’t repeat what he said, but with a large expletive, he said, “You really did it this time, you’re either out or something is wonderful for you, I don’t know. We’re ordered to send you right back.” And I went to London and put on the other wing with the other wing, and flew the rest of the war as a Yank.
